 A kink in the Social Security Administration’s payment calendar means no SSI benefits are being issued in November 2026.
 Europa Press William Allen Journalist and translator, AS USA About the author British journalist and translator who joined Diario AS in 2013. Focuses on soccer – chiefly the Premier League, LaLiga, the Champions League, the Liga MX and MLS. On occasion, also covers American sports, general news and entertainment. Update: Oct 31st, 2026 06:00 EDT 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Several million Americans got an early benefits payment on Friday , as the Social Security Administration (SSA) issued next month’s Supplemental Security Income (SSI) two days ahead of its usual schedule.
 Why was November’s SSI paid out in October?
 A benefit with just over 7.3 million recipients across the U.S., SSI is typically paid out on the first of each month. However, if that date is a federal holiday or a weekend day, the SSA brings distribution forward to the nearest business day before then. 
 As November 1 is a Sunday - and October 31 also falls on the weekend - the agency was forced to send out next month’s SSI on October 30 . SSI will then revert to its regular payment timeline in December, when program benefits are scheduled to go out on Tuesday 1.
 As a result of this minor quirk in the SSA’s distribution calendar , SSI benefits are still being paid out for November, but none will actually be issued in November .
 How much are SSI benefits in 2026? 
 Average payment as of Sep. 2026 : $735.86 
 Maximum individual payment in 2026: $994 
 Maximum payment for couples in 2026: $1,491 
 Maximum essential-person payment in 2026: $498 
 Some SSI beneficiaries can also claim a monthly supplement from their state. What’s more, the SSA has announced a 3.6% rise in SSI benefits in 2027 , starting with January’s program payment. 
 This cost-of-living adjustment will push the maximum individual payment up to $1,029 per month , the agency says, with the top couples’ benefit rising to $1,544 per month.
 View this post on Instagram 
 Who is eligible for SSI in the U.S.?
 A needs-based program, SSI is aimed at low-income, low-resource people who are over 65 or have a disability . Unlike the SSA’s Social Security scheme - which pays benefits to workers depending on their payroll-tax contributions - SSI eligibility is not contingent on an applicant’s work record.
 Find out more about SSI’s eligibility criteria in this explainer , or check out the SSA website .
